title: Acid + base: making salt and water
summary: Hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide neutralise each other.

reactants.title: Reactants
reactants.caption: Hydrochloric acid (HCl) and sodium hydroxide (NaOH). In water they are really ions (H⁺, Cl⁻, Na⁺, OH⁻); here they are drawn as simple units so we can follow the atoms.

approach.title: Acid meets base
approach.caption: The acid and the base come together.

break.title: Partners separate
break.caption: Hydrogen leaves chlorine, and sodium leaves the hydroxide group (OH).

form.title: New partners form
form.caption: Hydrogen joins hydroxide to make water, and sodium joins chlorine to make salt. The key change is H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O.

products.title: Products
products.caption: Water (H₂O) and sodium chloride (NaCl, table salt). This is a neutralisation reaction. It is mildly exothermic: about −57 kJ per mole of water formed.

notes.mechanism: Simplified model. In solution, NaOH and NaCl are not molecules but separate ions surrounded by water molecules. The thin white bonds are a schematic way to show ionic attraction.
notes.thermo: ΔH ≈ −57.1 kJ per mole of water for a dilute strong acid with a strong base.
